summary: Ngulchu Dharmabhadra (1772–1851) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery under Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen, and taught numerous students including Ngulchu Yangchen Drubpai Dorje.

Nguyen Thi Tuyet is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Punjabi University under doctoral supervisor Inder Mohan Singh, and also studied under traditional teacher Thich Nu Bao Nguyet (attested 2012).
Nguyen Thi Xinh works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed her PhD at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).
Nguyen Van Hoa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University, where he was supervised by Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre.
Nguyen Van Thuong specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi, where his MA was supervised by Karam Tej Singh Sarao.
Nhu Lien specializes in Buddhist studies. She studied at the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University under the teacher Ādiccavaṃsa.

Nianzu Huang (1913–1992) studied Buddhist studies, attending Beijing Institute of Technology (~1932–1936) and studying under several teachers including Lianju Xia and Hsu Yun. He headed the Central People's Broadcasting Station and was a professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (~1953–1980).

Nichidatsu Fujii (1885–1985) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who founded Nipponzan-Myohoji. He studied at Rissho University, Taisho University, Koyasan University, Horyuji Kangakuin, and Kennin-ji, and taught Gyoryo Maruyama.

Nicholas Dirks (born 1950) is an Indologist and historian. He studied at Wesleyan University (~1968–1972) and the University of Chicago (~1972–1981), and held posts at Caltech (~1982–1987), the University of Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia University (~1997–2013).

Nicholas Justin Allen (1939–2020) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies under Rodney Needham at the University of Oxford, where he served as Reader in Social Anthropology from 1976 and held posts at Wolfson College.

Nicholas Roerich (1874–1947) was a scholar and artist in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Imperial Academy of Arts, founded the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute, and directed the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts.
Nicholas Witkowski specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from Stanford University in 2015 and served as a research fellow at the University of Tokyo (attested 2017).
Nicholson T. Collier specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths.

Nicola Bajetta is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied as a doctoral local researcher at the University of Hamburg, where he was also a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter (attested 2026).

Nicola Di Cosmo (born 1957) is a sinologist and historian who earned his PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (~1985–1991). He taught at Harvard University (1993–1997) and became the Henry Luce Foundation Professor at the Institute for Advanced Study (~2003).

Nicolaas Johannes Krom (1883–1945) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served with the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (1913–1916) and held academic posts at Leiden University in 1919 and from 1925 to 1945.

Nicolaas van Wijk (1880–1942) was a linguist who studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1898–1902) and Moscow State University (~1902–1903). He held a post at Leiden University from 1913 and taught F. B. J. Kuiper.
Nicolas Morrissey is an Indologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Gregory Schopen (attested 2004). He holds a post at the University of Georgia.

Nicolas Revire works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Silpakorn University (2012–2013) under supervisors including Peter Skilling and Claudine Bautze-Picron, and held a post at Thammasat University (attested 2016–2017).

Nicolas Sihlé works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant professor in the Department of Anthropology at the University of Virginia (attested 2010; attested former 2026) and taught Jay Holt Valentine.
